references.text: Matthew's parallel account where many possessed people were brought to Jesus in the evening, and he cast out the spirits and healed all who were sick.
Mark's parallel account that when the sun set, they brought all the sick and possessed to Jesus, and he healed many.
Jesus laid hands on a few sick people and healed them, illustrating his practice of laying on of hands for healing.
Jesus laid hands on a woman who was bent over and healed her, another example of healing through the laying on of hands.
Paul laid hands on a sick man and healed him, a practice that reflects Jesus' method of healing by laying on of hands.
Jesus healed all kinds of diseases and afflictions among the people, demonstrating his power over various illnesses (ποικίλαις νόσοις).
Jesus promised that believers would lay hands on the sick and they would be made well, continuing his practice of healing.
Jesus' programmatic declaration in Nazareth where he announces his mission to heal and preach, now being fulfilled in practice in Capernaum.
Power went out from Jesus and healed everyone, emphasizing his ability to heal each individual who was sick.
Jesus had deep compassion for the sick and healed them, showing his care for every person.
